transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Lopez, Ethan Park (Redwood); Lina Chen, Raj Patel, Zoë Martin, Tomás Rivera (SkyForge)

Summary: Quick intro + mapping integration surface area for a joint GPU onramp. High-level agreements around pilot, security needs, and data flows. Redwood to run perf baseline and give checklist.

Topics covered: partner value, deployment modes, security/compliance, pilot criteria, pricing models, next steps

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Lopez: hey everyone thanks for joining uh excited to meet the SkyForge team, i'm Maya, account lead at Redwood. little bit of a quick agenda, we wanna understand your goals and constraints and sketch a pilot.
[00:14] Lina Chen: thanks Maya yeah i'm Lina, i run cloud partnerships at SkyForge. quick note, we're exploring some channel partner models and also a deeper integration where we surface Redwood inference as an onramp for our enterprise customers.
[00:29] Ethan Park: hi all, Ethan here, se on Redwood side. i'll mostly cover technical fit, perf expectations, and what the pilot would look like.
[00:36] Raj Patel: raj here - lead architect. we manage a mix of edge racks and centralized regions, most of our current infra runs on custom images with nvidia drivers, containerd, and a weird flavor of kv cache that we call kv-cash internally so apologies if i say that wrong.
[00:53] Tomás Rivera: hi, tomás - i'm on edge ops, network constraints are the big thing for us, a lot of 4G/5G backhaul to mid-tier colo.
[01:02] Maya Lopez: got it. so first question, what's the target customer for this integration? is it enterprise customers looking for low-latency inference at the edge, or is it more partner-managed deployments?
[01:15] Lina Chen: primarily enterprise, yes, low-latency inference near data. but also some of our smaller saas ISVs want a simpler managed path so a mix. timeline wise we want a pilot by q4 and broader go-to-market early next year.
[01:29] Ethan Park: perfect, that lines up with the typical runway we see. can you summarize minimum success criteria for pilot? like latency SLO, throughput, cost target?
[01:40] Raj Patel: sure, for the pilot we want p99 latency under 120ms for short-form generations (~128 tokens), 1k qps sustained across 3 racks, and cost per 1k tokens to be within 30% of our current baseline. also security: we need SSO/SAML for console, audit logs retention for 12 months, and KMS integration for customer keys.
[02:08] Ethan Park: ok we can hit those targets with dedicated pools and some batching knobs; we have an optimize toolkit that suggests quantization profiles. quick note—our runtime supports prefix caching and continuous batching, although on 4G backhaul sites you'll see variance.
[02:25] Raj Patel: when you say continuous batching, is the broadcast cache held local or remote? we want local KV to avoid round trips.
[02:33] Ethan Park: good question. our KV implementation can be pinned local in private deployments; in hosted onramp it's typically cached at the edge gateway but we can support a hybrid mode. just to note, sometimes docs call it KV cash in older notes, so apologies for the confusion, it's the same thing.
[02:49] Lina Chen: on security — can you support HSM-backed KMS? some customers require hardware keys.
[02:55] Maya Lopez: yes, Redwood Private supports HSM integrations and we can pass the KMS key reference for customer-owned keys. for hosted, we provide customer-managed KMS options via the private control plane.
[03:07] Tomás Rivera: network egress is also a concern. can Redwood compress or batch tokens to reduce transit? our sites have metered egress.
[03:14] Ethan Park: we do some client-side buffering and request coalescing; we also recommend model variants that are quantized to reduce token size. not a perfect cure but helps.
[03:23] Zoë Martin: procurement question — what's the commercial model if SkyForge wants to resell Redwood as an onramp? revenue share? per-token MSRP?
[03:33] Maya Lopez: flexible. we offer a channel partner price with revenue share or a fixed reseller discount plus uplift. we can pull together sample math. for pilots we typically do a trial credit and then committed capacity for dedicated pools.
[03:45] Raj Patel: another technical ask — we'd like a canary/fallback policy if a heavy model triggers latency spikes. can Redwood automatically fallback to a smaller variant?
[03:55] Ethan Park: yes, we have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; you can configure policy by latency threshold or cost. we also do per-route tracing and tracing hooks so you can see when fallbacks occur.
[04:08] Lina Chen: nice. are there any integrations with our billing system? we need cost reporting per-tenant.
[04:15] Maya Lopez: console gives token-level cost breakdown and per-tenant reporting; we also have an API to pull usage metrics so your billing system can ingest it.
[04:23] Tomás Rivera: okay technical detail: our edge racks sometimes run in air-gapped mode for regulated customers. is there an on-prem package?
[04:32] Ethan Park: yes, Redwood Private can be deployed on-prem with a private control plane; it supports air-gapped environments with offline package installation. note though, some features like hosted analytics need a connectivity path or a proxy that batches logs to the control plane.
[04:48] Zoë Martin: compliance — do you have SOC 2 and ISO certs? our procurement requires at least SOC 2 type II.
[04:56] Maya Lopez: we are SOC 2 Type II compliant and have ISO alignment — i will attach the current certs. we also provide audit logs for retention windows you configure.
[05:07] Raj Patel: for the perf baseline, what telemetry do you need from our side?
[05:12] Ethan Park: ideally: sample model, typical input length distribution, representative hardware matrix (GPU models, memory), network topology, and a small set of test prompts for reproducibility. we'll run a 24-48 hour run across a subset of racks.
[05:25] Lina Chen: ok sounds reasonable. Raj and tomás will collate config.
[05:29] Maya Lopez: on the partnership side, a few questions from our GTM team: do you want co-branded docs and joint webinars? and how do you prefer lead sharing to work?
[05:40] Lina Chen: yes co-branded assets are good. lead sharing we prefer a lead-to-revenue share approach with privacy filters; we can draft a simple MOU.
[05:50] Ethan Park: quick clarification on deployment: if we do a co-managed onramp on SkyForge colo, who manages upgrades?
[05:57] Raj Patel: our preference is SkyForge handles OS and drivers, Redwood handles model runtime and inference stack. upgrades would be coordinated.
[06:06] Maya Lopez: that aligns with a split responsibility model we often use. i'll draft an ops runbook that maps responsibilities.
[06:13] Tomás Rivera: also, about monitoring — can we get per-rack health streams?
[06:18] Ethan Park: yes per-node metrics are available via Prometheus exporters or we can push to your observability endpoints.
[06:26] Lina Chen: anything we should be cautious about?
[06:29] Ethan Park: the main caveats are: cold-starts for large models on smaller GPUs, and network jitter affecting p99 at edge sites. we can mitigate both with pre-warming and local KV pinning.
[06:42] Raj Patel: is there a limit on model families you support? we run a mix of LLaMA variants and some internally-tuned models.
[06:50] Ethan Park: we onboard open model families and custom models; we have an onboarding checklist that covers compatibility, tokenizers, and model format conversion. sometimes tokenization differences cause small output drift.
[07:04] Zoë Martin: procurement — is there a minimum committed spend for dedicated pools?
[07:09] Maya Lopez: yes typically a three or six month commit for dedicated pools, but we can be flexible for strategic partners. i'll include sample commitment tiers.
[07:18] Lina Chen: great, can you also share references or case studies for channel integrations?
[07:23] Maya Lopez: absolutely, i'll share two references—one from an edge telco partner and one from an enterprise SaaS that resold our onramp.
[07:32] Raj Patel: for the perf test schedule, can we aim for next week window? engineers are available 7/18-7/20.
[07:39] Ethan Park: yep i put 7/18 as target for the perf kickoff in the action items.
[07:44] Lina Chen: ok last thing — legal wants to know how data residency flows if a customer demands EU-only processing.
[07:52] Maya Lopez: we can pin model serving to EU regions in the private deployment or dedicated pools; with VPC options and customer-managed keys to satisfy residency and encryption requirements. i'll include a residency note in the checklist.
[08:06] Zoë Martin: perfect. that covers it for us.
[08:09] Maya Lopez: awesome, thanks everyone. quick recap of next steps: i'll send the one-pager, Ethan will send perf plan, Raj will share configs, Zoë will confirm procurement/NDA. we'll reconvene after perf results to scope the pilot.
[08:24] Lina Chen: thanks everyone talk soon.
[08:27] (meeting ends)
